NFPA 72.question: Fire alarm / releasing panel(s) show NORMAL; no fire, supervisory or trouble condition.
No unexplained isolations, inhibits or disabled functions are present.
FiberSystem 8000 linear heat detection controller healthy; no channel / fibre fault indication.
Flame detectors clean, unobstructed and correctly aimed at the protected belt / structure.
COBRA air purge panel healthy; compressor / purge air available; no purge fault.
Manual call points / manual release stations accessible, intact and clearly labelled.
Sounders / beacons / local annunciation devices intact and unobstructed.
Accessible field cables, glands, conduit and junction boxes visually sound.
Housekeeping, signage and access to equipment satisfactory.

NFPA 25.question: Deluge / water spray control valve and trim are in the correct normal set position; no visible leakage.
Water / air pressure gauges (where provided) are in the normal operating range.
Water supply isolation valves are open and secured / supervised.
Accessible pipework, fittings, hangers and supports show no leakage, impact damage or severe corrosion.
Open spray nozzles are correctly aligned and free from obstruction, paint or damage.
Strainers, drains and test connections are externally sound; no visible leakage.
Protected belt and support structure areas show no new obstructions that could block spray coverage.

NFPA 72.question: Fire alarm / releasing panel(s) show NORMAL; no unresolved fire, supervisory or trouble condition.
Review panel, controller and HMI event history since the last inspection.
Panel / controller time and date are correct.
No unexpected isolations, bypasses or inhibits are present.
Mains AC supply healthy; charger / PSU indication normal.
Battery condition satisfactory; no swelling, leakage or terminal corrosion.
FiberSystem 8000 controller healthy; no relay, communication or fibre channel fault.
Accessible fibre optic sensor cable route, supports and protection intact.
Flame detector windows clean; detectors unobstructed and aimed correctly.
COBRA air purge panel status normal; compressor operation acceptable.
Purge intake filters, regulator and tubing visually satisfactory.
Detector brackets / mounts secure; no unauthorised field-of-view changes.
Manual call points / manual release stations accessible, labelled and intact.
Sounders, beacons and annunciators intact and unobstructed.
Apollo loop interfaces / switch monitors / output units show normal status.
Functional test one representative initiating device / zone input and verify alarm response.
Test one representative MCP / manual release or monitored interface input (no unwanted discharge).
Verify sampled cause-and-effect outputs, annunciation and shutdown interfaces operate correctly.
Housekeeping, signage, legends and access to equipment satisfactory.

NFPA 25.question: Control valves are in the correct position and secured / electrically supervised.
Deluge valve and external trim are clean, intact and free of leakage.
System pressure gauges are in the normal range.
Water supply condition satisfactory; monitored supply status normal where provided.
Accessible pipework and fittings show no leakage, impact damage or unacceptable corrosion.
Hangers, braces and pipe supports are secure.
Open spray nozzles are correctly aligned and unobstructed.
Nozzle blow-off caps / shields intact where fitted.
Strainers, drains and test connections externally sound.
Flow / tamper / pressure supervisory devices visually intact.
Local manual release and emergency isolate interfaces accessible and labelled.
Release solenoids, pilot lines and associated actuators visually sound.
Check for plant / structural changes that could obstruct designed spray coverage.
Test one representative supervisory / alarm input associated with the water spray / deluge system.
Record defects, impairments and corrective actions required.

NFPA 72.question: Fire alarm / releasing panel(s) show NORMAL; no unresolved trouble condition.
Review alarm, supervisory and trouble history since the previous quarter.
Verify panel / controller time-date and communication links are correct.
Mains AC supply healthy; charger / PSU indication normal.
Measure and record battery float voltage.
Panel enclosure, labels, legends, drawings and access controls satisfactory.
FiberSystem 8000 controller healthy; review channel readings / trend information.
Accessible fibre optic sensor cable, junctions and supports show no damage.
Verify fibre controller zone mapping and alarm / trouble relay outputs.
Flame detectors clean, unobstructed and aimed correctly.
Perform OEM built-in test or approved functional test on representative flame detectors per zone.
Detector fault / dirty-optics supervision normal or verified during testing.
COBRA enclosure, compressor, purge tubing and fittings satisfactory.
Purge filters serviced / cleaned as required; airflow / pressure acceptable.
Apollo loop modules, switch monitors and output units identified and healthy.
Test representative monitor / output unit operation and feedback.
Test representative sounders / beacons / annunciation devices.
Test representative manual call point / manual release stations.
Verify sampled inputs and outputs report correctly at panel / HMI / SCADA.
Accessible field cables, glands, JB seals and earthing / bonding visually sound.
Release inhibit / test mode procedures used correctly and fully reinstated.
Housekeeping, signage and log book satisfactory.
All sampled devices restored and the system returned to NORMAL.

NFPA 25.question: Inspect control valves, locks, seals and electrical supervision.
Inspect deluge valve trim, releasing trim, solenoids and pilot lines.
Record and compare water / air pressures with previous logs.
Carry out main drain / alarm line test where the system arrangement permits.
Conduct a partial trip or release test of a selected zone using approved test arrangements.
Verify waterflow / alarm / supervisory signals at the fire panel / SCADA.
Accessible pipework, fittings, hangers and supports are sound.
Inspect nozzles for damage, corrosion, blockage and alignment.
Verify spray coverage paths to belt, drives, idlers and structure remain unobstructed.
Inspect strainers, drains and test valves externally.
Inspect manual release stations and local release cabinets.
Verify release output circuits, solenoids and monitored feedback during testing.
Valve rooms / cabinets / enclosures are clean, dry and serviceable.
Signage, valve tags and identification labels are present and legible.
Review impairments, previous defects and pressure trends.
Check availability of critical spare nozzles / seals / tools where site standard requires.
Reinstate all release devices, isolations and supervisory functions after testing.
Record defects, recommendations and corrective maintenance required.

NFPA 72.question: Review latest drawings, zone charts, cause-and-effect matrix and previous service reports.
Fire alarm / releasing panel(s) show NORMAL; no unresolved trouble condition.
Verify panel indicators, controls, legends and operator functions.
Mains AC supply and charger / PSU operation satisfactory.
Perform battery test in accordance with OEM / NFPA 72 requirements.
Inspect and clean panel cabinet, terminations and internal condition as required.
Verify configuration records, firmware versions and current backup information.
Test communication paths to remote annunciation / SCADA / BMS / fire control room where used.
Carry out FiberSystem 8000 annual functional checks in accordance with OEM guidance.
Review fibre system event history, temperature trends and recorded faults.
Inspect accessible fibre optic cable route, supports and physical protection along the conveyor system.
Test fibre controller alarm, pre-alarm and trouble outputs.
Test 100% of installed flame detectors by approved annual method / OEM self-test.
Clean detector windows / optics and verify aiming / field of view.
Verify flame detector fault / dirty-optics supervision.
Service COBRA air purge panels: filters, compressor operation, tubing, enclosure and PSU/battery condition where fitted.
Test 100% of manual call points and manual release stations.
Test 100% of monitored input / output modules used for release, flow, tamper and shutdown functions.
Test 100% of sounders, beacons and local annunciation devices.
Verify each tested initiating device produces the correct text, alarm sequence and cause-and-effect response.
Verify release inhibit, test mode, shutdown and restoration logic.
Inspect accessible field cables, terminations, gland seals and earthing / bonding.
Confirm signage, labels and drawings reflect the installed system.
Review false alarms, unwanted trips and outstanding defects for trend analysis.
Confirm required spares, tools and specialist test equipment availability.
Restore all tested devices, clear logs and return the system to NORMAL.
Handover outstanding defects / recommendations to site representative.

NFPA 25.question: Inspect control valves and supervisory devices; verify correct position and operation.
Inspect deluge valve externally and internally during outage / annual service where included in the maintenance plan.
Inspect and clean strainers, filters and orifices as applicable.
Perform full trip test of each deluge / releasing zone using controlled discharge or approved test arrangement.
Verify waterflow alarms, release outputs and shutdown interlocks operate correctly.
Measure and record static and residual pressures at test points.
Inspect water supply pipework, feed lines and sectional isolations.
Inspect open spray nozzles for obstruction, damage, corrosion and correct type / location.
Verify nozzle alignment and spray coverage to belt, head / tail / drive areas and supporting structure.
Inspect hangers, braces, supports and signs of mechanical damage.
Inspect drains, test headers and relief / drip points.
Inspect manual release devices and local release cabinets.
Inspect solenoids, pilot / releasing lines and trim components.
Inspect corrosion, scale or leakage at valves and fittings.
Verify valve signage, identification and operating instructions.
Review system impairments, leaks and pressure trends over the last year.
Verify spare nozzles, wrenches and trim kits are available where required.
Confirm post-test drainage / drying and corrosion prevention controls where applicable.
Check interfaces to monitored water supply equipment / pump start signals where provided.
Confirm protected areas have not changed in a way that compromises spray coverage.
Restore all valves, trips and supervisory devices to their normal state.
Record defects, corrective actions and recommendations.

general.question: Is the service label signed and current?
Is the service log book / maintenance record updated?
Is the fire protection system restored to the required AUTO / NORMAL state?
Are access ways, pull stations and valve stations unobstructed?
Have all defects / impairments been reported for corrective action?
